metaData.originalTitle: 你的 Agent 每次都“失忆”？这个工具彻底治好了我的前端开发焦虑
metaData.title: Your Agent Always "Loses Memory"? This Tool Completely Cured My Frontend Development Anxiety
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: OpenViking is an Agent memory hub centered on the MCP protocol, using structured memory extraction, intent analysis, and hierarchical retrieval to solve the problem of broken context in frontend development across sessions, agents, and platforms.
metaData.summary: This article, published by the ByteDance technical team, introduces their open-source Agent memory management tool, OpenViking. It starts from the common pain point of frontend developers using AI Agents: "memory loss" — the Agent cannot inherit context across sessions, tools, or SubAgents, forcing developers to repeatedly describe design specifications and historical decisions for each collaboration. OpenViking uses the MCP protocol to connect with tools like Trae, Codex, and Claude Code, automatically extracting and structurally storing four types of memory during conversations: entities, events, preferences, and profile. Its recall mechanism employs a two-stage strategy of "intent analysis + hierarchical retrieval": first, it uses an LLM to understand the user's task intent, then routes the query to the corresponding level of the memory tree for recursive search. The article demonstrates the complete workflow through a case study of "building a product Playground webpage," covering everything from automatic specification sedimentation, one-sentence recall, incremental specification addition, to the final effect comparison. Finally, it provides the MCP configuration steps and rule templates for integrating OpenViking into Trae.

mainPoints.point: The core bottleneck of Agent collaboration is the lack of a structured, cross-session long-term memory foundation.
mainPoints.explanation: Current AI Agent tools have isolated sessions, preventing design specifications and historical decisions from being inherited, forcing users to repeatedly describe context, making the Agent less effective over time.

mainPoints.point: OpenViking acts as the Agent's memory hub via the MCP protocol, enabling cross-tool memory sharing.
mainPoints.explanation: It connects with tools like Trae, Codex, and Claude Code, automatically extracting and structurally storing four types of memory (entities, events, preferences, profile) during conversations.

mainPoints.point: Its recall mechanism uses a two-stage strategy of 'intent analysis + hierarchical retrieval,' rather than simple keyword matching.
mainPoints.explanation: It first uses an LLM to understand the user's task intent, then routes the query to the corresponding level of the memory tree for recursive search, improving recall accuracy.

mainPoints.point: Cross-session, cross-SubAgent, and cross-platform memory sharing is the core value of OpenViking.
mainPoints.explanation: Multiple sessions, SubAgents, or different Agent tools within the same project can share a single project memory, preventing context breaks and style inconsistencies.

keyQuotes: You're not using an AI tool — you're feeding a goldfish that forgets everything every morning.
True AI collaboration should understand you better the more you use it, not require you to reintroduce yourself every time.
OpenViking is the 'memory hub' connecting you and all your AI Agent tools.

relatedArticles.title: A Game Within a Game! Equipping Agents with OpenViking, They Actually Learned to 'Hold Grudges' and 'Disguise'?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces ByteDance's open-source OpenViking context management framework and its companion VikingBot, vividly demonstrating through a multi-agent Werewolf game demo how to provide Agents with long-term, traceable collective memory, enabling them to learn across games, form strategies, and simulate complex social behaviors.

relatedArticles.title: How to Make Your Agent More Accurate: MCP Tool Design Best Practices
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores the core mindset shift in AI Agent tool design, proposing that tools should be viewed as the 'user interface' for Agents rather than traditional API wrappers, and details design guidelines for naming, descriptions, and inputs based on the MCP protocol.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Douyin Dynamic Experience Optimization: Practices and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details Douyin's self-developed dynamic performance framework DDPF, systematically explaining how on-device intelligence and dynamic scheduling technologies address performance optimization challenges in complex business scenarios, covering framework design, perception and decision-making, and virtual machine tuning.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Coze 3.0 Officially Launched: A New Generation AI Team Starts with Coze
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Coze 3.0 is officially launched, upgrading Agent from a single-point tool to a collaborative AI team through project spaces, multi-device collaboration, and a skill store, ushering in a new way of human-Agent collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Making Douyin Smooth on Old Phones: The Three Things We Got Right
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: ByteDance shares deep low-level optimization practices for old Android devices across three dimensions: memory (ART heap expansion), FD (breaking the 1024 limit), and threading (M:N user-mode threads).
